//overrides: postcss/sharp: next 16.2.12 vendors postcss 8.4.31 and sharp 0.34.5, both
carrying HIGH advisories with no fixed next release. Lifting them here is
what makes `npm audit --omit=dev` clean (Issue #131). Drop these once next
The postcss floor is ^8.5.26 rather than the ^8.5.23 that first cleared the
postcss advisory because postcss is also how nanoid reaches the runtime tree:
8.5.23 ranges on nanoid ^3.3.16, and 3.3.16 carries GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (HIGH).
8.5.26 is the first release to require nanoid ^3.3.17. Keep the floor at or
above 8.5.26 so a fresh resolve cannot land back on a vulnerable nanoid.
eslint-plugin-react-hooks: eslint-config-next floats this on a caret range;
hydration patterns in hooks/use-mobile.ts and components/ui/date-range-picker.tsx.
Pinned to the version the lockfile already used so the rule change lands in
its own PR with the refactor, not bundled into unrelated work.
//typescript: Read this as a floor and a ceiling that are set by two different things.
Floor: DefinitelyTyped records a minimum compiler per package in
`typeScriptVersion`, and every type package declared here now sits at 5.6
(@types/node 26, @types/react 19.2.18, @types/react-dom 19.2.4, @types/pg
8.21 — they converged; this used to be @types/node alone). 6.0 clears it.
Ceiling: `~6.0` rather than `^6.0` is deliberate and is the tighter of the
two constraints. typescript-eslint 8.66.0 declares a peer of
`>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`, so `^6.0` would permit 6.1.x — a compiler the lint
toolchain does not claim to support. `~6.0` yields >=6.0.0 <6.1.0, which is
that ceiling exactly. This is not arbitrary tightness: it is the same rule
#215 set when the range was `^5.6`, where the caret ceiling (<6.0.0)
happened to fall inside the peer range on its own. Under a 6.x floor it no
longer does, so the ceiling has to be stated rather than inherited.
Re-derive both ends when a type package moves or typescript-eslint widens
its peer range (Issue #215).
Expect two typescripts in the lockfile. `tsconfck` (via vite-tsconfig-paths)
declares `peerOptional typescript ^5.0.0`, which 6.0.3 does not satisfy, so
npm nests a second copy at 5.9.3 under vite-tsconfig-paths. It is dev-only
and used only to parse tsconfig for vitest path resolution — nothing type-
checks against it. vitest already reports the plugin as redundant (vite
resolves tsconfig paths natively via `resolve.tsconfigPaths`), so dropping
it removes the duplicate; that is a test-resolution change and belongs in
its own PR, not bundled into a compiler bump.
Why not 7: TypeScript 7 is the native port and does not expose the JS
compiler API `next build` drives for its type-check pass, so Next 16.2.12
cannot host it (PR #246). It is also outside typescript-eslint's peer
range. Both have to move before 7 is reachable; .github/dependabot.yml
ignores the major in the meantime.
//eslint: Held on 9.x. Unlike the `~6.0` typescript pin above, the range needs no
tightening — `^9` already means >=9.0.0 <10.0.0, which is the ceiling we
want — so this note is the whole of the constraint: it records that the
caret is load-bearing rather than incidental, and must not be widened to
`>=9` or bumped to `^10` on the assumption that a lint bump is routine.
ESLint 10 removed the deprecated rule-context accessors (context.getFilename()
and friends, superseded by context.filename in 8.40) and the plugins
eslint-config-next vendors still call them, so 10.x crashes at rule-load
time before linting a single file. eslint-plugin-react peers at ^9.7,
eslint-plugin-import and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y at ^9, eslint-plugin-react-hooks
at ^9.0.0; eslint-config-next 16.3.0 still requires eslint-plugin-react
^7.37.0, whose only satisfying release is the same 7.37.5. There is no
version of the Next lint config that runs on ESLint 10 (PR #247).
9.39.5 carries npm's `maintenance` dist-tag, so this is a supported line,
not a stale one. Issue #263 is the tracker. It used to be #194, on the
reading that this pin and the non-blocking build-time `npm audit` gate were
one upstream event: npm's only offered fix for the HIGH advisories in the
eslint 9 dev tree was eslint@10, so the gate could not close until this
moved. That reading was wrong, and worth recording because it is the easy
one to reach again — those advisories were patched *within* the ranges the
lockfile already resolved (brace-expansion 1.1.18/5.0.9, js-yaml 4.3.1,
picomatch 2.3.2, fast-uri 3.1.5), the gate is blocking as of #194, and this
pin outlived it. The plugin peer ranges above are now the whole of the
constraint. Lift once eslint-config-next ships ESLint 10-compatible plugins
— eslint-plugin-react > 7.37.5 is the one to watch; .github/dependabot.yml
ignores the major in the meantime.
